newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brokers change rating on Elf stock.
newsitem.headline: Brokers change rating on Elf stock.

text.p: Research firm Detroyat Associes cut its rating on French energy group Elf Aquitaine to minus from plus, while broker Dupont-Denant raised its recommendation on the stock to buy, portfolio managers said on Friday.

They said Dupont-Denant raised its estimates on Elf profits, to seven billion francs for 1996 from six billion previously and to 8.2 billion francs for 1997 from 6.9 billion. They said it cited Elf's improved business mix and cost-cutting programme.
Detroyat raised its EPS estimate for Elf for 1996 but cut it for 1997 on expectations of lower crude prices and modest growth in petrochemicals.
It raised its EPS estimate to 24.40 francs from 21.60 for 1996 but lowered it to 24.70 francs from 22.90 for 1997.

Brokerage SGE Delahaye on Thursday switched its rating to outperform from neutral on Elf shares after the company reported a 24 percent rise in first-half net attributable profit to 3.56 billion francs.
Elf shares were up 0.3 percent at 379.50 francs at 1400 GMT.
